source.name: Knight Frank & ANAROCK research compiled via ETRealty & industry reports

areas.name: South Bengaluru
areas.meaning: The largest market, but the longest reported sell-through period (7.4 quarters). High existing inventory creates favorable negotiation conditions for buyers.

microMarkets.name: Electronic City
microMarkets.buyerAction: Abundant ready and near-completion inventory. Buyers have substantial bargaining room on base pricing and waiver of parking/amenity add-ons.

microMarkets.name: Kanakapura Road
microMarkets.buyerAction: Substantial launch volume following metro connectivity. Multiple competing developers provide strong leverage to negotiate flexible payment milestones.

microMarkets.name: Bannerghatta Road
microMarkets.buyerAction: Pink Line metro construction is a mid-term catalyst; focus on projects with clear RERA completion dates within 12-18 months.

microMarkets.name: JP Nagar & Jayanagar Peripheral
microMarkets.buyerAction: Infill micro-market with lower new supply additions. Price resilience is higher; discounts are narrower compared to further south.

areas.name: East Bengaluru
areas.meaning: Strong absorption with 4.9 quarters to sell. Healthy velocity, but heavy ongoing launches require comparing developer balance sheets and execution records.

microMarkets.name: Whitefield
microMarkets.buyerAction: Metro operational impact already priced in. High launch pipeline means buyers should prioritize Grade-A developers with strong delivery track records.

microMarkets.name: Sarjapur Road
microMarkets.buyerAction: Substantial ongoing launches. Prioritize projects with confirmed Cauvery water connections and check road widening timelines.

microMarkets.name: Varthur & Panathur / ORR Catchment
microMarkets.buyerAction: Extremely high tech rental yield demand; absorption moves fast. Inspect internal approach road widths and flood/lake buffers before committing.

microMarkets.name: Budigere Cross / OMR
microMarkets.buyerAction: Fast emerging with major township projects. Excellent airport/highway access, but social infrastructure is still maturing.

areas.name: North Bengaluru
areas.meaning: Fastest growing corridor (+11% sales YoY) with the lowest overhang (3.9 quarters). Strong momentum driven by airport and tech infrastructure expansion.

microMarkets.name: Hebbal & Bellary Road
microMarkets.buyerAction: High demand, low overhang. Ready-to-move units command stiff premiums. Buyers face limited discount margins on Grade-A supply.

microMarkets.name: Thanisandra & Jakkur
microMarkets.buyerAction: Proximity to Manyata Tech Park sustains absorption. Check feeder road widths and pending flyover/metro link works.

microMarkets.name: Bagalur & KIADB Aerospace Park
microMarkets.buyerAction: Significant launch pipeline from major developers. Good for long-term horizon (5+ years); verify BWSSB water line execution and actual commercial leasing pace.

microMarkets.name: Yelahanka & Doddaballapur Road
microMarkets.buyerAction: Mature green belt with limited new land parcels. Resale market is stable; lower risk of sudden supply spikes.

areas.name: West Bengaluru
areas.meaning: The published corridor data is too thin to call this area hot or cold. Low inventory (2,291 units) reflects limited land parcels rather than low buyer interest.

microMarkets.name: Yeshwanthpur & Rajajinagar
microMarkets.buyerAction: High land scarcity keeps supply tight. Evaluate redevelopment project credentials and layout approvals carefully.

microMarkets.name: Tumkur Road & Peenya Periphery
microMarkets.buyerAction: Price-sensitive segment. Assess industrial proximity and distance from main commercial hubs.

areas.name: Central Bengaluru
areas.meaning: Very little comparable public volume is reported. Very tight inventory (187 units) with bespoke pricing not comparable to broader suburban corridors.

microMarkets.name: CBD / Indiranagar / Koramangala
microMarkets.buyerAction: Pricing is determined by bespoke developer branding and micro-locality prestige rather than city-wide inventory statistics.
